Dissimilarity from a long table

Source: R/vegdist.R
el_vegdist.Rd

Computes the distance from a table without zeros. The query is run by DuckDB and written to a temporary Parquet file sorted by taxon. A compiled kernel then reads it in batches and adds up the shared quantities for every pair of samples, so the memory used is the result (one number per pair of samples) plus one batch.

Usage

el_vegdist(
  x,
  method = c("bray", "jaccard", "euclidean", "aitchison", "manhattan", "canberra",
    "robust.aitchison"),
  binary = FALSE,
  pseudocount = 1,
  ropt = 3,
  samples = NULL,
  batch_rows = 1e+06,
  threads = NULL,
  memory_limit = NULL,
  sample = "sample",
  taxon = "taxon",
  quant = "quant"
)

Arguments

x

A data frame or lazy duckplyr table with one row per non-zero sample and taxon. Rows with quant == 0 are ignored, but a sample that has only such rows is kept as an all-zero sample. Negative values are allowed only for method = "euclidean" without binary, for example after el_decostand(method = "rclr").

method

One of "bray", "jaccard", "euclidean", "aitchison", "manhattan" and "canberra", as in vegan::vegdist(). "aitchison" is the Euclidean distance between clr-transformed samples, computed from the counts. "canberra" is NA, as in vegan, between two all-zero samples. "robust.aitchison" is the Euclidean distance on the robust clr with the zeros filled by matrix completion (rank ropt, as in vegan). It needs counts, and no all-zero samples.

binary

If TRUE, use presence and absence instead of quantities.

pseudocount

For method = "aitchison" only: added to the counts before the clr. A positive number, "inverse_depth" for 1 / (the sample's total count), or a positive numeric vector named by sample. The unit is that of the counts, so give raw counts, not relative abundances. "inverse_depth" uses the totals of the table passed in, so after filtering taxa it is not the depth of the whole library: compute the depths first and pass them as a named vector.

ropt

For method = "robust.aitchison" only: the rank of the matrix completion, 3 as in vegan. A whole number below the number of samples and of taxa.

samples

Optional vector of all sample IDs, which also sets the order of the result. Samples in samples that are absent from x are treated as all zero. Without it, the samples that occur in x are used, in alphabetical order.

batch_rows

Approximate number of table rows held in R at a time. A batch always holds whole taxa.

threads

Number of threads for the pair kernel. Defaults to the option ecolongr.threads, or half of the cores. The result does not depend on it.

memory_limit

Memory DuckDB may use for sorting the table, such as "250MB"; it spills to disk beyond that. Defaults to the option ecolongr.memory_limit, or "250MB". This is separate from the memory used by R for the result and the current batch.

sample, taxon, quant

Names of the columns in x.

Value

A dist object.

Details

Euclidean distance on el_decostand(method = "rclr") output reads absent cells as 0. That is not vegan's "robust.aitchison" when the table has zeros, because vegan first fills them by matrix completion; see el_decostand().

Examples

library(dplyr)

# A long table of read counts for 16S ASVs in a time series from the Baltic Sea.
counts <- duckplyr::read_csv_duckdb(
  system.file("extdata", "lmo_free_living.tsv.gz", package = "ecolongr"),
  options = list(delim = "\t", header = TRUE), prudence = "stingy"
)
metadata <- read.delim(system.file("extdata", "lmo_free_living_samples.tsv", package = "ecolongr"))

# Samples with at least 5,000 reads.
deep <- counts |>
  summarise(reads = sum(quant, na.rm = TRUE), .by = sample) |>
  filter(reads >= 5000) |>
  select(sample)
counts <- semi_join(counts, deep, by = "sample")
metadata <- filter(metadata, sample %in% as.data.frame(deep)$sample)
d <- counts |>
  el_decostand("total") |>
  el_vegdist("bray", samples = metadata$sample)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpXIBetp/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.

# A dist object, so base R and vegan work on it.
hc <- hclust(d, "average")
head(cutree(hc, k = 4))
#>  LMO_2011-2023_16S:P2256_1001 LMO_2011-2023_16S:P17302_1014 
#>                             1                             1 
#>  LMO_2011-2023_16S:P2256_1002 LMO_2011-2023_16S:P17302_1015 
#>                             1                             1 
#> LMO_2011-2023_16S:P17302_1016  LMO_2011-2023_16S:P2256_1003 
#>                             1                             1 
head(cmdscale(d, k = 2))
#>                                      [,1]        [,2]
#> LMO_2011-2023_16S:P2256_1001  -0.36373842  0.09539471
#> LMO_2011-2023_16S:P17302_1014 -0.25660013  0.09419716
#> LMO_2011-2023_16S:P2256_1002  -0.38406749  0.01317695
#> LMO_2011-2023_16S:P17302_1015  0.04824488 -0.23368001
#> LMO_2011-2023_16S:P17302_1016 -0.24735047  0.05039300
#> LMO_2011-2023_16S:P2256_1003  -0.38311115 -0.06718847

# Aitchison distance from the raw counts, with a pseudocount of 1 / library size.
d_aitchison <- counts |>
  el_vegdist("aitchison", pseudocount = "inverse_depth", samples = metadata$sample)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpXIBetp/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
round(cor(d, d_aitchison), 2)
#> [1] 0.35
